Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the third inning of this riveritng test match. The umpires are on the field and so are the players of New Zealand. Michael Bracewell will take the field for Blair Tickner as he did in the first inning of West Indies. Brandon King and John Campbell to open for the Cherons. Jacob Duffy has the new red cherry in his hand. Let's play...
... THIRD INNING ...

After the loss of Conway's wicket, Daryl Mitchell and Mitchell Hay forged a great 5th wicket partnership, adding more 73 runs to the Kiwis. Mitchell Hay got his maiden half-century and it's been a special inning for the 25-year-old. Well, after their partnership broke up, the tailenders did well enough to get a small partnership and stretched the lead to 73 runs. On the other end, the Chevrons didn't have a goot first session, where they only picked two wickets, but after the Lunch break, they made a comeback.

New Zealand finishes their first inning with having a lead of 73 runs. Looking at the pitch, it is not offering any major impact on the deliveries, but in the pitch report, according to the experts, they said that it will open up as the match progresses. New Zealand's top order batted well and provided some crucial runs, especially Devon Conway, scoring 60 off 108 deliveries.

The Windies' bowling has been a bit inconsistent, hasn't it? Tight lines, but also some wayward deliveries that gave the Kiwis' batters opportunities to hit boundaries. Kane Williamson certainly took advantage of that. Roach and Anderson Phillip have had some success with their nagging length, and it's likely the Windies will stick to that plan in the next session. The Kiwis will be looking to capitalize on the Windies' inconsistency and build on their strong position but if WI can hit the right areas, there is a lot in the deck for the bowlers. We will be back by 12.05 am GMT.

A dropped catch can be a costly affair, and Brandon King would be kicking himself for letting Conway off the hook. Conway's been looking solid, and he's well-positioned to take the Kiwis to a strong total. With 55 runs under his belt, he's got the momentum, and the rest of the batting order will be looking to add to the total as well. The Kiwis are definitely in the driver's seat, and it's going to be interesting to see how the Windies try to turn the game around.

Anderson Phillip's delivery that got him was absolute magic! Commentary.Commentary: Day 2 is about to get underway, and Tom Latham and Devon Conway are back at the crease, looking to build on their solid start. The Kiwis are off to a steady start, and they'll be keen to keep the momentum going. Kemar Roach is bowling the first over of the day. Let's see how the Kiwis respond to the challenge. Unfortunate news for New Zealand fans, Blair Tickner has dislocated his left shoulder and will not be featuring in this game.

The stage is set for a thrilling day of Test cricket, with New Zealand looking to take a commanding lead. The first session of play will be crucial, and the team that comes out on top will be well-placed to dictate the course of the game. The Windies will be looking to produce a magical spell and rip through the top order, while the Black Caps will be focused on building a solid foundation. It's shaping up to be an enthralling contest, and fans are in for a treat.

The West Indies will come out with renewed energy on day two, looking to exploit any early morning swing or seam movement. Their premier fast bowlers will be looking to break the overnight partnership swiftly and expose the middle order to the new ball as quickly as possible. The Black Caps, on the other hand, will be focused on survival and consolidation, aiming to navigate the tricky initial period and then accelerate their scoring rate as the day progresses and the ball softens. The top order batters will need to show resilience and patience to build an imposing total that can realistically ensure their team moves into an unassailable position.

In response, New Zealand's openers, Tom Latham and Devon Conway, showed remarkable composure to see out the tricky final overs of the day, finishing at 24 for no loss. This solid start has given the Black Caps a slight edge heading into day two, and they will be looking to build on this momentum. The focus will be on converting this strong position into a match-defining lead, and with all ten wickets in hand, the Black Caps have the perfect platform to build a truly formidable total. A significant first-innings lead will be crucial in determining the course of this game, putting immense pressure on the West Indies' batting line-up in their second innings.

The scene is set for a captivating second day of the 2nd Test match between New Zealand and the West Indies, with the Black Caps looking to build on their strong position. The West Indies were bowled out for a modest 205 runs, thanks to a disciplined bowling attack from the Black Caps. Blair Tickner and Michael Rae were in superb form, swinging the ball and finding the edges, while the other bowlers maintained the pressure, leaving the Windies struggling to cope. Despite flashes of resilience from the top order, the West Indies were unable to capitalize on their early momentum, and the Black Caps' bowlers reaped the rewards.

That's a wrap on Day 1! The Kiwis have dominated proceedings, bowling out the West Indies for 205 and heading into the break without losing a wicket. A brilliant day for New Zealand, and the momentum is certainly with them. Looking forward to seeing what Day 2 brings. The action resumes at 10 pm GMT (previous day), with the buildup starting an hour earlier. Thanks for tuning in, cheers!

New Zealand pacer Michael Rae shared his thoughts on his impressive debut performance, revealing that he had received the news of his potential inclusion just a couple of days ago, and the past few days had been surreal for him. He expressed his excitement to have taken his first wicket in Test format and acknowledged that he had learned a thing or two during the day, adjusting his game at the right time to bag a few wickets, and was thrilled to have pulled one back and caught the edge, with Daryl taking it safely. Rae attributed his success to his pace, stating that he is a bit quicker than many, which gave him confidence, and praised the West Indies batters, saying they are excellent cricketers who would punish any mistakes. He lauded his fellow bowlers, Jacob Duffy, and Zakary Foulkes, who had bowled beautifully but were unlucky to not get many wickets, and felt that bowling out the West Indies on the first day and getting to bat on the same day was a good feeling, crediting Tom Latham for his honest and consistent messaging, which helped the team reap rewards in the last session.

In reply to the West Indies' first innings total, the Kiwis' openers, Tom Latham and Devon Conway, got off to a solid start, putting on 24 runs together in 9 overs without giving the Windies' bowlers much to celebrate. They're looking comfortable at the crease, and if they can continue to build on this foundation, the Kiwis could be in a great position. A solid opening partnership will be crucial, and if they can get it right, it could set the tone for the rest of the innings.

The injury to Blair Tickner will be a major concern for the Kiwis. Blair Tickner probably dislocated his shoulder while trying to save runs at fine leg is a significant blow, especially considering how crucial pacers' injuries were in the previous game. With Tickner's availability in doubt for the rest of the game, the Kiwis will be relying heavily on their batters to provide a healthy cushion.

The lower order tried to put in the hard yards and show some grit, but they couldn't add much despite chewing up a few deliveries. Glenn Phillips' dismissal of Tevin Imlach made inroads into the tail, and the rest of the tail failed to add significant runs. The New Zealand bowlers' pressure and precision ultimately paid off, restricting the West Indies to 205 all out.

The West Indies' batting lineup showed promise, but ultimately fell short. Shai Hope, John Campbell, Brandon King, and Roston Chase all got starts but were dismissed at crucial moments, preventing them from capitalizing on their good beginnings. Blair Tickner's superb bowling was instrumental in breaking through the Windies' batting order, claiming 4 wickets. Michael Rae also had an impressive performance, taking 3 wickets.

Stumps on Day 1 and what a day it's been! The West Indies were put in to bat and started strong, thanks to John Campbell and Brandon King's 66-run opening partnership. However, they lost two wickets at the same score, taking some of the momentum away. The middle order tried to steady the ship, with Shai Hope top-scoring with 48, but unfortunately, the batters below him struggled to contribute significantly, leading to a disappointing total of 205 all out.
